prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on what kind of plan you need (Medicare, ACA/individual & family, small‑group/employer, etc.), whether you want in‑person help, your preferred carriers, and how much ongoing support you want. I can help you find good local options if you tell me a few details, but first here’s how to pick a great broker and what to ask.

Quick questions so I can narrow it down
- What type of coverage? (Individual/Family on the Marketplace, Medicaid/CHIP, Medicare, small‑group employer plan, or something else)
- ZIP code (or Kansas City, MO vs Kansas City, KS)
- Do you want in‑person meetings, or is phone/online OK?
- Any language preferences, doctors you need in‑network, or special needs (prescriptions, chronic conditions)?

How to choose a great Kansas City broker
- Use an independent broker/agent who represents multiple carriers so you get a shopping comparison, not just one insurer.
- Verify they’re licensed in Missouri and/or Kansas (depending on where you live) via the state insurance department.
- For Medicare help, look for AHIP certification or CMS/Medicare training and ask about experience with Medicare Advantage, Part D, and Medigap.
- Check online reviews (Google, Yelp), and ask for references from other clients.
- Ask how they’re paid (most get commissions from insurers; some charge a fee). Confirm there are no hidden costs and whether they’ll help after enrollment with claims or renewals.
- Prefer brokers who provide enrollment assistance and year‑round support (not just during open enrollment).

Questions to ask a broker during a quick interview
- Which carriers do you work with locally?
- How many clients like me have you helped?
- Do you charge a fee or do you work on commission?
- Will you help with claims and plan renewals after I enroll?
- Can you provide client references or online reviews?

Where to look
- State insurance department license lookup (Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance; Kansas Insurance Department) to confirm licensing and any complaints.
- NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) membership can indicate professionalism.
- HealthCare.gov broker/assister directories for Marketplace enrollment help.
- Local independent agencies and brokers listed on Google/Yelp with high ratings.

If you want, I can:
- Look up well‑rated independent brokers/agencies in Kansas City if you give your ZIP and plan type.
- Suggest specific questions tailored to Medicare, ACA, or employer plans.
Tell me your zip and what type of coverage you need and I’ll find some local brokers you can call.
